newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OSCE head of mission expelled from Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: OSCE head of mission expelled from Chechnya.

text.p: Chechen authorities said on Tuesday they had expelled the head of mission of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), criticising him for calling Chechnya part of the Russian Federation.

"The Foreign Ministry of the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria considers the further presence of (Tim) Guldimann on the territory of Chechnya to be inadmissible," the statement signed by the self-styled foreign minister said.
The document was distributed by the press secretary of current President Zelimkhan Yandabiyev, who leaves office next week after having lost the January 27 presidential election to Aslan Maskhadov.
An OSCE spokeswoman in Vienna said Guldimann, a Swiss diplomat, had left the Chechen capital, Grozny, for the neighbouring region of Ingushetia.
"(He) is waiting it out for the next few days to see what happens. He expects that when the new government takes office this will be reversed," she said.
Itar-Tass news agency, quoting a source in President-elect Maskhadov's team, said Maskhakov backed Guldimann.
"Guldimann acted in strict observance of the mandate of the OSCE and could still exert considerable influence in regulating relations between Chechnya and Russia," the source said.

Russia withdrew is remaining forces last month from Chechnya, marking the end of an military campaign launched in 1994 to crush a Chechen drive for independence. Chechnya is now seeking formal independence but Moscow refuses any concession on sovereignty.

According to a member of the presidential guard, Guldimann was ordered to leave Chechnya by 5:30 p.m. (1430 GMT) on Tuesday. Four cars from the presidential guard were seen leaving the OSCE compound at about 5 p.m.

Guldimann declared the January 27 presidential election in Chechnya free and fair. But in their statement Chechen authorities criticised remarks Guldimann made at a news conference in Moscow last week.
"During this press conference, Mr. Guldimann stated that the OSCE considers the Chechen republic of Ichkeria a part of the Russian Federation," it said.

"Moreover, Mr. Guldimann has declared that Chechen leaders were accepting the OSCE position with this understanding and were allowing the OSCE mission to work on Chechen territory in this spirit," it said. "Such a position of the OSCE offends the Chechen people and state and contradicts the principles agreed between Russia and Chechnya."
The statement demanded an explanation from the OSCE on its official position on the status of the Chechen republic and the issue of what it called war crimes by Russian forces.
A total of 72 OSCE observers watched the Chechen vote, giving it a seal of respectability many Chechens viewed as important in its bid to win full independence from Moscow.
